line: Anything you're looking forward to in the next few weeks?
followUps: What are you most excited about with that?
How did that come about?
shareBack: Offer one thing you're looking forward to, in a sentence, then ask what else is coming up.

line: I need something new to watch. What's the last thing you couldn't stop watching?
followUps: What hooked you about it?
Would I like it, do you think?
shareBack: Mention the last thing you watched and whether you'd recommend it, then ask for one more pick.

line: What's been the best part of your week so far?
followUps: What made that so good?
Is that a regular thing or a one-off?
shareBack: Offer one small good thing from your own week, then ask what's left on their week.

line: Eaten anywhere good lately? I'm stuck in a rut.
followUps: What did you have?
How did you find it?
shareBack: Mention one place you keep going back to, then ask if they've been.

line: Got anything fun planned for the weekend, or is it a do-nothing one?
followUps: How did that plan come about?
What does a good do-nothing weekend look like for you?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what your weekend looks like, then ask what they'd do with a spare day.

line: Settle something for me: plan a vacation down to the minute, or just show up and see?
followUps: Has that ever gone badly wrong for you?
What's the best trip you've had that way?
shareBack: Say which camp you're in and one time it backfired, then ask where they'd go next.
deliveryCue: Say it playfully; it's a fun argument, not a quiz.

line: You seem like you're in a good mood today. Did something go right?
followUps: What happened?
Has it been that kind of week overall?
shareBack: Mention one thing that's gone right for you lately, then hand it back with a question.
deliveryCue: Only if they really do. Say it with a smile.

line: If we both had next weekend completely free, what would you want to do?
followUps: What's stopping us from actually doing that?
When did you last do something like that?
shareBack: Offer your own pick in a sentence, then suggest a date to actually do one of them.

line: How did you get into this, by the way? I've never asked.
followUps: What keeps you coming back?
What was it like when you first started?
shareBack: Say in a sentence how you ended up here yourself, then ask what they'd tell a beginner.
deliveryCue: For a shared class, club, gym, or hobby.

line: Have you been here before? I'm still working out what's good.
followUps: What would you go for?
How did you first find this place?
shareBack: Mention a similar place you like, then ask if they know it.

line: This was a great pick, by the way. How did you find this place?
followUps: What else around here do you like?
Do you come here a lot?
shareBack: Mention one spot you'd pick next time, then ask if it sounds like their kind of thing.

line: How do you know the hosts? I'm still working out who everyone is.
followUps: How long have you known them?
Who else here should I meet?
shareBack: Say how you know the hosts in a sentence, then ask for a good story about them.

line: Have you tried the food yet? Tell me what's worth going back for.
followUps: What was the best thing on the table?
Are you a cook yourself, or happily not?
shareBack: Mention what you've tried and liked, then ask what they'd bring to a party like this.

line: I feel like I only ever see you at these things. We should fix that.
followUps: What are your weeks like right now?
Would a coffee or a walk suit you better?
shareBack: Offer one concrete idea and a rough time, then ask what would work for them.
deliveryCue: Say it warmly, then make a real suggestion.

line: What have you been getting into lately, outside the usual routine?
followUps: How did that start?
What do you like most about it?
shareBack: Mention one thing you've picked up or want to try, then ask how they'd start.

line: Last time you said you had something coming up. How did it go?
followUps: What was the best part?
Would you do it again?
shareBack: Mention something similar you've done or want to do, then ask what they'd recommend.
deliveryCue: Use it when you remember something they mentioned.

line: What's the best thing you've done this year so far?
followUps: What made that one stand out?
Is there more like it planned?
shareBack: Offer your own highlight in a sentence, then ask what they'd still like to fit in this year.

line: What's been taking up most of your head lately?
followUps: How long has that been going on?
What would make it easier?
shareBack: Mention one thing that's been on your own mind, briefly, then go back to theirs.
deliveryCue: Listen first; don't jump to fixing.

line: I was thinking the other day about that first trip we took together. What do you remember most?
followUps: What do you think we'd do differently now?
Should we do something like that again?
shareBack: Offer the one moment you remember best, then ask which trip of ours was their favorite.

line: What are you looking forward to that I don't know about yet?
followUps: When did that come up?
What are you hoping it'll be like?
shareBack: Offer something you haven't told them about yet, in a sentence, then ask what comes after that.

line: I've got a decision I keep going around in circles on. Can I talk it through with you?
followUps: What would you do in my place?
Have you ever had to make a call like this?
shareBack: Lay it out in a minute or two, thank them, then ask what they're weighing up right now.
deliveryCue: Keep your side short so it stays a two-way talk.

line: I meant to say, the way you handled that whole situation really impressed me. How did you stay so calm?
followUps: Was it as hard as it looked?
What did you learn from it?
shareBack: Say what you'd have done in their place, honestly, then ask how it's sitting with them now.
deliveryCue: Name the actual situation so it's specific.

line: Is work still as intense as it was, or has it calmed down?
followUps: What's the part that's draining you most?
Is there an end in sight?
shareBack: Mention in a sentence how your own work has been, then ask what they do to switch off.

line: You've seemed a little quiet lately. No pressure, but I'm around if you want to talk.
followUps: Do you want to talk about it, or would a distraction help more?
What would help this week?
shareBack: Mention only that you've had stretches like that too, then leave the space for them.
deliveryCue: Only if you've noticed it. Say it once, gently.

line: What are you wrestling with right now? Big or small.
followUps: What's making it hard to decide?
What does your gut say?
shareBack: Offer one thing you're wrestling with too, briefly, then return to theirs.
deliveryCue: Listen; don't fix unless they ask.

line: What are you quietly proud of from this year?
followUps: What did it take to get there?
Who else knows about that?
shareBack: Tell them something you've noticed them do well this year, then offer one of your own.

line: I still laugh about the worst night out we ever had. Which one would you pick?
followUps: What on earth were we thinking?
Who else was there that night?
shareBack: Add the one detail you remember that they might have forgotten, then ask for another story.

line: What do you want more of in your life right now?
followUps: What's getting in the way of it?
What would a first small step look like?
shareBack: Offer one thing you want more of yourself, in a sentence, then ask how you could help with theirs.
deliveryCue: Fine if the answer is 'sleep'. Let them choose how deep to go.

line: I think you've changed over the last few years, in a good way. Do you feel it?
followUps: What do you think caused it?
Is there anything you miss about how you were before?
shareBack: Name one specific change you've seen in them, then say one way you think you've changed too.

line: What have you changed your mind about as you've gotten older?
followUps: What changed it for you?
Do you think you'll change your mind again?
shareBack: Offer one thing you've come round on, in a sentence, then ask what they still won't budge on.

line: Is there anything you wish we did more of, you and me?
followUps: What do you miss most from when we saw each other more?
When could we actually do that?
shareBack: Say one thing you'd like more of with them, then pick a date together.

line: I've been thinking about what I want the next few years to look like. Do you ever do that?
followUps: What's on your list?
What would you want to be different by then?
shareBack: Offer one thing on your own list, briefly, then ask what's on theirs that might surprise you.

line: You've been a really good friend to me this year and I don't say it enough. Have I been showing up for you?
followUps: What's one thing I could do better?
When did you most need someone this year?
shareBack: Name one specific time they helped you, then ask what would help them most right now.
deliveryCue: Mean it, and take the answer without defending yourself.

line: Is anything worrying you that you haven't really talked through with anyone?
followUps: How long has it been on your mind?
Do you want ideas, or just someone to hear it?
shareBack: Offer a worry of your own only after they've finished, and keep it short.
deliveryCue: Listen; don't fix.

line: What do you think we'll be like when we're old? I'm hoping still doing this.
followUps: What do you hope we never stop doing?
Where do you picture yourself living by then?
shareBack: Describe your own picture of it in a sentence, then ask what they'd want to have done by then.
deliveryCue: Works lightly or seriously; follow their tone.

line: You're in charge of the music. Put on something you've had on repeat.
followUps: Where did you first hear this?
What does it remind you of?
shareBack: Queue one of your own next and say in a sentence why, then ask for another of theirs.
deliveryCue: In the car or at home, with music handy.

line: What's the best road trip you've ever done?
followUps: What made it so good?
What went wrong along the way?
shareBack: Offer one road trip memory in a sentence, then ask where they'd drive if they had a free week.

line: I love what you've done with this room. What made you go for it?
followUps: What was it like before?
What's next on the list?
shareBack: Mention one thing you'd like to change at your own place, then ask for their advice on it.
deliveryCue: Point at the specific thing you like.

line: What are you cooking these days? I need new ideas.
followUps: Where did you get that one from?
What's your no-effort dinner?
shareBack: Mention one thing you make too often, then ask what they'd add to it.

line: That was a beautiful ceremony. Which part got you?
followUps: Had you heard that story about them before?
What are you looking forward to tonight?
shareBack: Mention the moment that got you, then ask how long they've known the couple.
deliveryCue: At a wedding or similar ceremony.

line: Days like this always make me think back. What's your favorite memory of us with this crowd?
followUps: Who else was there for that?
What do you think has changed most since then?
shareBack: Offer your own favorite in a sentence, then ask who they've been hoping to see today.

line: Okay, show me something from where you are. What's on your desk right now?
followUps: What's the story behind that?
Is that where you spend most of your day?
shareBack: Hold up something from your own side and say what it is, then ask what they'd change about their space.
deliveryCue: On a video call, while it is still warming up.

line: I'm glad we finally made this happen. What's been the best part of your month?
followUps: What made it good?
What's coming up next month?
shareBack: Offer your own best part in a sentence, then ask what else they've been up to.

line: What have I missed since we last talked? Start with the good stuff.
followUps: How did that come about?
And what's been the harder part?
shareBack: Give your own one-line update, then go back to the thing they sounded most excited about.

line: I can't believe it's you. I was thinking about you just the other day. What brings you here?
followUps: How long are you around for?
Do you get over this way much?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what brought you here, then ask if they have time for a real catch-up soon.
deliveryCue: Lead with how glad you are to see them.

line: It's so good to see you. What's keeping you busy these days?
followUps: How long have you been doing that?
Are you enjoying it?
shareBack: Give your own one-line version, then ask about the part they sounded happiest about.

line: What are you into these days? Last I knew, you were deep into something new every month.
followUps: What happened to the old ones?
What got you into this one?
shareBack: Mention one thing you've got into since you last saw them, then ask what they'd recommend trying.

line: Do you still see anyone from the old crowd?
followUps: How are they doing?
When was the last time we were all in one room?
shareBack: Mention who you've kept up with, then ask who they'd most like to see again.

line: I was hoping you'd be here. What's the headline from your last couple of years?
followUps: How has that changed things for you?
What's been the best part of it?
shareBack: Give your own headline in a sentence, then ask about the thing they mentioned first.

line: I'm really glad we ran into each other. I've thought about getting in touch more than once.
followUps: What's the best way to reach you these days?
Would you be up for a real catch-up soon?
shareBack: Say plainly that the gap wasn't about them, then suggest one easy way to meet.
deliveryCue: No need to explain the gap at length.

line: I still think about the place we always used to end up at. Have you been back?
followUps: What do you miss most about those days?
Is anywhere near you like it now?
shareBack: Offer one small memory from there, then ask what their version of that place is now.

line: This made me think of you. No reply needed, I just had to send it.
followUps: Have you seen anything like it before?
What's the best thing anyone's sent you this week?
shareBack: If they reply, say in a line why it reminded you of them, then ask what they're up to.
deliveryCue: Attach the photo, link, or song.

line: That was fun the other night. Let's do it again. Any evening good for you next week?
followUps: Same place, or somewhere new?
Who else should we ask along?
shareBack: Offer two evenings that suit you, then let them pick.

line: You mentioned a show the other day and I've forgotten the name. What was it?
followUps: Where can I watch it?
Anything else like it you'd recommend?
shareBack: Once you've tried it, text back one thing you liked, then ask what they're on to next.

line: How did the thing you were getting ready for go? I've been wondering.
followUps: Which part went best?
Are you relieved it's done?
shareBack: Reply to their answer first; then add one line about your own week and ask what's next for them.
deliveryCue: Name the actual thing if you remember it.

line: I'm near that place you told me about. What should I order?
followUps: What do you usually get?
Want to come next time?
shareBack: Text back a quick verdict afterwards, then suggest going together.

line: A few of us are getting together this weekend. Want to come along?
followUps: Which day suits you better?
Anyone you'd like to bring?
shareBack: Give the time and place in one line, then say it's fine either way.

line: What you said the other day has stuck with me. Where did you pick that up?
followUps: Has it changed how you do things?
What else has stuck with you like that?
shareBack: Say in a line how you've used it since, then ask what they've been thinking about lately.
deliveryCue: Quote the thing they said so it's specific.

line: Thinking of you today. How's this week treating you, anywhere from fine to chaos?
followUps: What's the chaos part?
Anything I can take off your plate?
shareBack: Give your own one-word rating and a line of why, then ask what would make the week better.

line: Just remembered the time we got completely lost on that trip. Still makes me laugh.
followUps: What do you remember about it?
Where should we get lost next?
shareBack: Add the detail that makes you laugh most, then ask what they're doing this weekend.

line: No agenda, just missing you. Got ten minutes for a call this week?
followUps: Which evening is easiest?
Or should I just try you on the off chance?
shareBack: Offer two times that suit you, then let them choose.

line: I never said it properly: thank you for being there when things were rough. It meant a lot.
followUps: How have things been on your side since then?
Can I buy you dinner to say it in person?
shareBack: If they reply, name the one thing they did that helped most, then ask how they are doing.
deliveryCue: Send it without expecting a reply.

line: Honest answer: how are you doing with everything on your plate right now?
followUps: What's the heaviest part?
Do you want company, a distraction, or just to vent?
shareBack: Keep your own news to a line; offer one specific thing you can do this week.
deliveryCue: Listen; don't fix.

line: Quick one, because I trust your judgment: can I run something past you later?
followUps: When's a good time?
Call or text, which is easier?
shareBack: Keep the ask short when you get to it, thank them, then ask what's going on with them.

line: Walked past our old spot today and thought of you. Hope life's treating you well. No need to reply.
followUps: Do you ever get back there?
What are you up to these days?
shareBack: If they reply, share one line about your life now, then ask one easy question about theirs.
deliveryCue: Send it and let it go; any reply is a bonus.

line: A song came on today that took me straight back to those car rides with you. Had to say hi.
followUps: Do you still listen to any of that?
What are you listening to now?
shareBack: If they reply, name the song and one thing you remember, then ask how they are doing.

line: Found an old photo of us and laughed out loud. Sending it over. Hope you're doing well.
followUps: Do you remember where this was?
Who took it, do you think?
shareBack: If they reply, say what you remember about that day, then ask what they're up to now.
deliveryCue: Attach the photo.

line: Someone told a joke today that only you would have appreciated. Made me miss you.
followUps: Want to hear it?
Who makes you laugh like that these days?
shareBack: If they reply, tell the joke, then ask one easy question about their week.

line: It's been forever, and that's on me too. I think of you more than I say. How's life, in one line?
followUps: What's the best part of it right now?
Would you be up for a call sometime?
shareBack: Give your own one-line version, then suggest a low-effort way to catch up.

line: Happy birthday! I still think about the one we celebrated together. Hope today's a good one.
followUps: Doing anything nice for it?
How did the year treat you?
shareBack: If they reply, share one line of your own news, then ask what they're looking forward to this year.
deliveryCue: Only on their birthday.

line: I'm going to be in your area next month. Any chance you'd be up for a coffee?
followUps: Which day would suit you?
Is there a place near you that you like?
shareBack: Give your dates in one line and say there's no pressure if the timing is bad.

line: I just made the recipe you taught me and it still works. Thank you, years later.
followUps: Are you still cooking it?
What are you making these days?
shareBack: If they reply, say who you cooked it for, then ask what's new with them.
deliveryCue: Swap in whatever they taught you or introduced you to.

line: I'm sorry I went quiet for so long. That's on me, not you.
followUps: What's been happening with you?
What's the easiest way to stay in touch these days?
shareBack: Give a one-line reason without making excuses, then ask what has been good for them lately.
deliveryCue: Say it once. No long explanation.

line: I never answered your last message, and I'm sorry. I'd love to hear how you've been.
followUps: What's been the best part of the last while?
Anything big I missed?
shareBack: Answer anything they ask, keep your own news to a line or two, then ask about what they sounded happiest about.

line: I think I was short with you last time we talked. Sorry about that. You didn't deserve it.
followUps: Are we okay?
How have things been since?
shareBack: If they ask, say what was going on for you in a sentence, with no excuse, then ask how they have been.
deliveryCue: Say it plainly, with no "but" after it.

line: I'm sorry I bailed on our plans. Can I make it up to you? Next one's on me.
followUps: What night works for you?
Same plan, or something new?
shareBack: Offer two times you can really do, then let them pick.

line: Sorry I missed your big night. I hate that I wasn't there. Will you tell me how it went?
followUps: What was the best moment?
Who else was there?
shareBack: Say in a line why you missed it, with no excuses, then suggest a way to celebrate together.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real event.

line: It's good to see you. I'm sorry we lost touch. I think that was mostly me.
followUps: What's been going on with you?
Do you still see anyone from back then?
shareBack: Give a one-line update on your life now, then ask about the part of theirs they lit up about.
deliveryCue: Keep it light. One line is enough.

line: I've thought about how things ended between us, and I'm sorry for my part. No need to reply.
followUps: How have things been for you?
Would you be open to a coffee sometime?
shareBack: If they reply, thank them first. Keep your own news short and let them set the pace.
deliveryCue: Send it once and don't push for an answer.

line: I've been replaying our argument, and I was wrong about my part. I'm sorry. Can we talk?
followUps: What was it like on your side?
What would help us move past it?
shareBack: Hear their side fully before adding anything, then say one thing you will do differently.
deliveryCue: Own your part only. No "but".

line: I hate how we left things. You matter more to me than being right.
followUps: Can we start over on it?
What do you need from me?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what you'd do differently, then ask what they'd like to happen next.

line: I know I hurt you, and I'm not going to explain it away. I'm sorry. I'm here when you're ready.
followUps: Would it help to talk about it?
Is there anything I can do now?
shareBack: Don't defend yourself. Say one thing you've learned, then leave the next step to them.
deliveryCue: Then give them time.

line: This is overdue, but I'm sorry for how I treated you back then. You didn't deserve it.
followUps: How have things been for you since?
Is there anything you'd want to say to me?
shareBack: Accept whatever they say without arguing, then ask one easy question about their life now.
deliveryCue: No excuses, and don't expect forgiveness on the spot.

line: Sorry about earlier. I was in a bad mood and took it out on you. That wasn't fair.
followUps: Are we good?
How's the rest of your day going?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what was really bothering you, then ask about their day.

line: It's really good to see you. I've been thinking about you.
followUps: Do you feel like talking, or would a distraction be better?
What's today been like?
shareBack: Skip your own news for now. Offer one specific thing you can do this week.
deliveryCue: Say it, then leave room. Silence is fine.

line: Thinking of you today. No need to reply.
followUps: What's today been like?
Would a call help, or just a few texts?
shareBack: If they reply, keep your side to a line and offer one small, specific thing you can do.
deliveryCue: Send it and let it be. Any reply is a bonus.

line: I'm going to the store tomorrow. What can I pick up for you?
followUps: Anything else this week?
Want me to just leave it at the door?
shareBack: Skip your own news. Confirm when you will come by, then let them go.
deliveryCue: A specific offer is easier to accept than "let me know."

line: No need to go into it. I just wanted you to know I noticed, and I'm around.
followUps: Do you want company, or some space?
Is there one thing that would help this week?
shareBack: Don't share a story of your own. Offer one specific thing, then let them choose.

line: That sounds really hard. I'm sorry you're dealing with it.
followUps: Do you want to talk about it, or would a distraction help more?
What's the hardest part right now?
shareBack: Don't compare it to your own troubles. Name one thing you could do, then follow their lead.
deliveryCue: Then leave room. You don't need to fill the silence.

line: Can I bring dinner over one night this week? You wouldn't have to host me.
followUps: Which night is easiest?
Anything you are craving, or anything to avoid?
shareBack: Name a night and a dish, then say it's fine to change their mind.
deliveryCue: Name the night if you can.

line: I'm free Saturday morning. Can I take something off your hands?
followUps: What's been piling up?
Would company help, or just the extra hands?
shareBack: Confirm a time and what you will bring, then leave it there.
deliveryCue: Swap in a time you can really do.

line: I heard you've had a rough stretch. I'm sorry. No pressure to talk about it.
followUps: Is there anything that would make this week easier?
Want to grab a coffee sometime, no agenda?
shareBack: Don't ask for details. Offer one small, specific thing and let them decide.

line: Want to grab a coffee after this? We don't have to talk about anything in particular.
followUps: Is there a place you like near here?
Same time next week, too?
shareBack: Talk about easy things unless they bring up what is going on. If they do, just listen.

line: If it helps, I can send you my notes from this week. Just say the word.
followUps: Anything else that would help with class?
Want me to save you a seat next time?
shareBack: Keep it practical. Ask what else would help, without asking for details.
deliveryCue: For a class or course you share.

line: Do you feel like talking about it, or would a distraction be better right now?
followUps: What would help most this week?
Is there one thing I could do?
shareBack: Follow whichever they pick. If they talk, listen; if not, suggest one easy thing to do together.
deliveryCue: Either answer is fine. Follow their lead.

line: I'd love to hear about them, if you feel like telling me.
followUps: What's a favorite memory you have of them?
What were they like?
shareBack: Share one memory of your own only if you knew them, then go back to listening.
deliveryCue: For a loss. Use the person's name if you know it.

line: No words needed. I'm here, and I'm not going anywhere.
followUps: Want me to call tonight?
Would a few silly texts help?
shareBack: Keep sending small, easy messages over the next week. Don't ask for updates.

line: Would a call help, or would you rather I just keep sending you silly things?
followUps: What time would be good for a call?
Any requests for the silly things?
shareBack: Do whichever they pick, and keep your own news to a line.

line: I know it's been a long time, but I heard what happened and I'm so sorry. Thinking of you.
followUps: Is there anything you need right now?
Would you be up for a call sometime?
shareBack: If they reply, listen and keep your side short. Offer one specific thing if it makes sense.
deliveryCue: Send it without expecting a reply.

line: I'm dropping some food at your door tonight. No need to answer it.
followUps: Any foods to avoid?
Want me to do the same next week?
shareBack: Leave it and go. Text later to say it's there, with no questions attached.

line: What's been keeping you busy lately, the good kind or the other kind?
followUps: Which kind is winning?
What would make the next few weeks easier?
shareBack: Give your own split in a sentence, then go back to the part they said most about.

line: Checking in. What's one good thing and one annoying thing from your week?
followUps: Want to vent about the annoying one?
How did the good one happen?
shareBack: Send your own good and annoying thing in a line each, then ask what is coming up.

line: You've had a lot going on lately. What's been the hardest part, and what's been okay?
followUps: How are you handling it?
Is there anything I can take off your plate?
shareBack: Keep your own news short. Offer one specific thing you could do.
deliveryCue: Listen. Don't fix unless they ask.

line: What's been weighing on you lately, if anything? Happy to just listen.
followUps: How long has that been going on?
What would help, even a little?
shareBack: Say honestly what has been on your own mind in a sentence, then go back to them.
deliveryCue: Ask when you have time to hear the answer.

line: Congratulations! I want the whole story. How did it happen?
followUps: When did you find out?
